heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
text: Rooted in Miami Gardens and shaped by the people who raised him, taught him, and stood by him, Oliver Gilbert is running to give back to the community that made him who he is. Raised in Miami Gardens, educated in local public schools, and shaped by a lifetime of service to his community, he is running to build a stronger future for South Florida.

heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
text: His story is one of faith, perseverance, and service — from supporting himself as a college student and riding the bus to law school, to leading his growing hometown as Mayor and bringing safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, to fighting as a County Commissioner for better public transit, housing people can afford, and economic growth that benefits the entire region — his focus has always been on creating stronger neighborhoods, more resilient communities, and a better future for working families.

heading: Rooted in Miami Gardens. Fighting for Our Future.
text: At every step, his purpose has remained the same: to bring opportunity home and build a South Florida where every family has a fair shot.

heading: Most people want the same things.
text: They want to get to work without losing half their day. They want to see a doctor without dreading the bill. They want their kids to inherit an economy that rewards effort.

heading: Their time back.
text: A two-hour commute isn’t a transit problem. It’s a family problem, a cost problem, and a life problem.

heading: Care they can afford.
text: Nobody should wait until it’s too late to see a doctor because of the bill. Coverage isn’t a luxury. It’s a foundation.

heading: A real shot.
text: Small businesses and working families built South Florida. They deserve a federal government that builds with them — not around them.

heading: Restore the American Dream.
text: The HOME Act lowers monthly housing costs without weakening lending standards — helping responsible families own a home, build generational wealth, and gain long-term financial stability.

heading: Restore the American Dream.
text: And for the families locked out the longest — first-time and working-family buyers — it opens three more doors: expanded FHA lending, a homebuyer tax credit, and a cap on starter rates.

heading: 01 / The Affordability Problem
text: Millions of families can afford a home. They just can't afford this month's payment.

heading: 01 / The Affordability Problem
text: Home prices and mortgage rates have pushed monthly payments beyond what many hardworking families can carry — even when their income, credit, and employment are strong. The usual "fix" is to loosen lending standards, which is exactly what fueled past housing collapses. The HOME Act rejects that trade-off: it lowers the monthly payment without lowering the standards that keep lending sound.

heading: Payments Outpace Paychecks
text: Monthly costs have climbed faster than wages, putting a first home out of reach for qualified buyers.

heading: A Closing Door
text: Families who could once buy are now locked out, delaying the wealth-building that ownership provides.

heading: The Wrong Fix
text: Weakening underwriting to close the gap creates risk. Sound lending should never be the price of access.

heading: 02 / How the HOME Act Works
text: The HOME Act keeps traditional underwriting and simply restructures repayment. You qualify the way you would today. Your total cost is fixed at closing using a standard 30-year calculation. Then you choose how long to spread that fixed cost — which lowers what you owe each month.

heading: Qualify the traditional way
text: Income, credit, employment, debt-to-income ratios, and appraisals are all evaluated under today's 30-year underwriting standards.

heading: Lock your total cost
text: At closing, your interest rate and total repayment obligation are fixed using a traditional 30-year mortgage calculation.

heading: Choose your schedule
text: Spread that same fixed cost over a 40, 50, or 60-year payment schedule — whichever fits your budget.

heading: Pay less each month
text: A longer schedule means a smaller required monthly payment — freeing up room in the family budget.

heading: Pay less each month
text: Same total repayment. A longer schedule. A smaller monthly payment.

heading: Pay less each month
text: Your total repayment obligation does not increase because you selected a longer payment period. The longer schedule lowers the monthly amount, not the math behind it.

heading: Pay less each month
text: Calculator not loading? Open it in a new tab .

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: Six principles hold the HOME Act together. Tap any item to expand.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: Borrowers qualify under existing 30-year underwriting standards. Income, credit, employment, debt-to-income ratios, and appraisals remain unchanged.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: The interest rate and total repayment obligation are fixed at closing. Borrowers choose a 40, 50, or 60-year payment schedule without increasing the total repayment obligation because of the longer schedule.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: Private lenders originate and service HOME mortgages. Treasury-backed housing bonds provide liquidity while participating lenders receive targeted federal tax credits.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: Qualified heirs may assume the mortgage without a forced refinance or interest-rate reset, preserving family stability.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: The HOME Act is paired with policies that increase housing production, streamline permitting, encourage workforce housing, support modular construction, and discourage institutional speculation.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: Families qualify at the traditional payment but benefit from a lower required payment, creating room to build emergency savings, retirement savings, education funds, home maintenance reserves, or small business capital.

heading: 03 / The Six Pillars
text: A lower required payment gives families room to breathe — to build emergency savings, retirement, education funds, home maintenance reserves, or the capital to start a small business.

heading: 04 / The First-Time Buyer Package
text: The HOME mortgage lowers the monthly payment. These three policies clear the other barriers — the down payment, the closing costs, and the rate itself.

heading: 04 / The First-Time Buyer Package
text: First-time buyers and working families face hurdles a lower payment alone can't fix: saving a down payment while paying rent, covering closing costs, and qualifying when rates spike. The HOME Act meets each one head-on. And every policy below follows the same rule as the HOME mortgage itself — more access, same sound lending standards.

heading: Expanded FHA Lending
text: FHA loans are how generations of American families bought a first home — low down payments, sound underwriting, and a public guarantee that makes lenders say yes. The HOME Act expands FHA lending for first-time buyers: loan limits that reflect what homes actually cost in communities like ours, lower mortgage-insurance premiums, and a simpler, faster approval process.

heading: Expanded FHA Lending
text: A first home with a down payment a working family can actually save.

heading: Homebuyer Tax Credit
text: A refundable federal tax credit for first-time and low-to-moderate-income homebuyers — real help with the down payment and closing costs that keep qualified families renting. The credit turns years of "almost enough" into keys in hand, and starts families building equity from day one.

heading: Homebuyer Tax Credit
text: Cash help at closing. Equity from day one.

heading: Capped Starter Rates
text: When interest rates spike, first-time buyers are the first ones priced out — families with strong income and credit watch the same house drift out of reach. The HOME Act caps the interest rate on qualifying first-time homebuyer mortgages, backed by the same public-private financing as the HOME mortgage: Treasury-backed bonds and lender tax credits cover the difference, so lenders stay whole and standards stay sound.

heading: Capped Starter Rates
text: The rate can't price a first family out of a first home.

heading: 05 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: A lower monthly payment. Expanded FHA lending. A first-time homebuyer tax credit. Capped starter rates. The HOME Act proves families don't have to choose between affordable payments and responsible lending. Add your support and help restore the American Dream.

heading: BUILD Business Act
text: America should not only be the best place in the world to work. It should be the best place in the world to start a business.

heading: BUILD Business Act
text: Small businesses are the backbone of the American economy. The BUILD Business Act modernizes the Small Business Administration by expanding access to capital, reducing barriers to entrepreneurship, and helping more Americans start, grow, and expand successful businesses.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: Too many entrepreneurs have the talent and determination to succeed but cannot access the capital needed to get started. The BUILD Business Act closes that gap by pairing affordable financing with mentorship, accountability, and streamlined government.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Eleven concrete actions to help Americans start, grow, and expand small businesses. Tap any item to expand.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Create the American Small Business Grant Program providing grants of $5,000 to $25,000 for equipment, inventory, software, licensing, insurance, lease deposits, and other startup costs.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Goal: Give entrepreneurs access to capital before debt becomes necessary.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Establish the SBA Growth Line offering low interest loans, generally from 0% to 2%, with deferred repayment.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Goal: Help growing businesses scale without being overwhelmed by early debt.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Strengthen the SBA 7(a) program by increasing federal guarantees, reducing borrower fees, simplifying approvals, speeding processing, and expanding lending in underserved communities.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Strengthen the SBA 504 program by expanding funding, modernizing eligibility, speeding project approvals, and creating a new 504 Express Expansion track for established businesses creating jobs.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Provide enhanced financing incentives for businesses that establish employee ownership and profit-sharing programs.

heading: 02 / My Plan

heading: 02 / My Plan

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Create one digital portal for grants, loans, mentoring, technical assistance, and contracting opportunities.

heading: 02 / My Plan

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Partner with universities, chambers of commerce, Small Business Development Centers, experienced business mentors, minority business organizations, and local economic development agencies.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Publish annual reports measuring business creation, job creation, survival rates, loan performance, and taxpayer return on investment.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Simplify procurement and help more small businesses compete for government contracts.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Goal: Create reliable customers, not just affordable financing.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Reduce paperwork, simplify reporting requirements, coordinate permitting where possible, and expand digital services.

heading: 02 / My Plan
text: Goal: Let entrepreneurs spend more time growing businesses.

heading: Real Help, Right Where You Are
text: Opening your first restaurant? Access startup grants and affordable financing.

heading: Real Help, Right Where You Are

heading: Real Help, Right Where You Are

heading: Why This Matters
text: The BUILD Business Act shifts federal policy from simply recruiting employers to creating more of them. When small businesses succeed, communities create jobs, families build wealth, neighborhoods become stronger, and America's economy grows from the ground up.

text: Require business plans for grant applicants.

heading: A Full Life. A Secure Future. A Promise That Lasts.
text: Every person with a lifelong disability deserves healthcare, a safe home, meaningful relationships, and the support to live with dignity throughout every stage of life.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: For millions of families, the hardest question is not what happens today. It is what happens tomorrow.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: Parents of children with intellectual, developmental, and other lifelong disabilities often spend decades serving as caregivers, advocates, benefits experts, transportation coordinators, housing planners, and emergency responders. They hold together a system that was never designed to work as one system.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: When a child becomes an adult, families can face separate rules for Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment services, transportation, and community programming. A parent may have to contact multiple agencies just to keep basic services in place.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: Then comes the question no family should have to face alone: What happens when the parent becomes sick, grows older, or dies?

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: Too often, the answer is a crisis. Housing is disrupted. Caregivers disappear. Benefits lapse. Siblings are asked to take over without preparation. Adults who have lived in the community may face isolation or unnecessary institutional placement.

heading: 01 / The Challenge
text: That is not a system of care. It is a system of uncertainty.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The CARE Act creates a comprehensive federal framework for lifelong care and community living. It brings existing programs together, fills the gaps between them, and ensures that every eligible person has one coordinated plan for life.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: No person should lose healthcare, housing, caregiving, or community because a parent can no longer provide care.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The CARE Act is built around eight commitments . Tap any item to expand.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: Every eligible person will have one federally certified CARE Advocate beginning during the transition to adulthood and continuing throughout life. The CARE Advocate becomes the family's single point of contact and coordinates services across Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, healthcare, transportation, employment, education, and community programs.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means One person responsible for making sure the whole system works together.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: Eligible individuals will receive timely access to necessary home and community-based services, including personal assistance, nursing, therapies, behavioral healthcare, transportation, respite care, supported employment, day services, residential support, and emergency backup care.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means Community care should be dependable, not something families wait years to receive.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The CARE Act will expand accessible housing modeled after successful efforts such as Casa Familia, including supported apartments, small shared homes, mixed-income communities, independent living options, and higher-support residences. Housing funding and care funding will be coordinated instead of treated as unrelated programs.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means The goal is not simply a bed. The goal is a home and a community.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: Community Belonging Grants will support programs that create real relationships and full community participation. That includes models similar to Friendship Circle, Best Buddies, Special Olympics, faith-based inclusion programs, arts, recreation, volunteer service, peer mentoring, and civic engagement.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means A full life includes friends, places to go, people who know your name, and opportunities to contribute.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: Beginning in adolescence, each participant and family will create a Lifelong Support Plan covering housing, healthcare, communication needs, transportation, employment, daily support, emergency care, financial planning, future caregivers, and supported decision-making. The plan will follow the individual and be updated over time.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means The transition after a parent's death should never begin with strangers trying to reconstruct a person's life.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The CARE Act expands respite care, caregiver training, mental health support, sibling planning, legal and financial guidance, emergency caregiver networks, and transition assistance.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means Parents should be allowed to be parents, not unpaid administrators of a broken system.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The plan invests in direct support professionals through better reimbursement, competitive wages, training, career ladders, benefits, recruitment, retention, and emergency staffing.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means A promise of care means little if there is no one available to provide it.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: The CARE Act will make assistive technology part of the basic support plan, including communication devices, smart-home systems, wearable health tools, remote monitoring chosen by the individual, adaptive robotics, mobility technology, accessible transportation, and digital care coordination.

heading: 02 / The CARE Act
text: What it means Technology should increase independence and safety without replacing human connection or personal choice.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: The CARE Advocate is the practical center of the plan. This person will not replace a parent, guardian, caregiver, doctor, or benefits agency. The advocate will make sure they are communicating and working from one coordinated plan.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Helps the individual and family create and update the Lifelong Support Plan.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Coordinates applications, renewals, and transitions involving Medicaid, Medicare, Social Security, housing, employment, and transportation.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Organizes annual meetings with the individual, family, caregivers, providers, and appropriate agencies.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Maintains an emergency and successor-care plan.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Tracks deadlines and prevents avoidable gaps in benefits or services.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Helps resolve disputes and escalates urgent needs when agencies fail to respond.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Monitors actual quality of life, not merely whether forms were completed.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Remains accountable to the individual and respects supported decision-making, privacy, choice, and independence.

heading: 03 / How the CARE Advocate Works
text: Federal agencies will retain their legal authority over eligibility and benefits. The CARE Advocate will have statutory coordination authority, access to participating agencies with the individual's consent, and the ability to require timely responses and elevate unresolved cases.

heading: 04 / One Lifelong Support Plan
text: Every participant will have one secure, portable Lifelong Support Plan recognized across participating programs. The individual must be at the center of that plan, with family and trusted supporters involved according to the individual's preferences and legal rights.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: The CARE Act will establish continuous coverage and coordinated care for people with qualifying lifelong disabilities. Medicaid will remain the principal payer for long-term services and supports. Medicare will cover eligible medical services. Social Security will provide income support. The CARE Advocate will make those systems function as one plan instead of separate bureaucracies.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Prevent unnecessary interruptions in Medicaid for people with permanent qualifying disabilities.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Provide Medicaid wraparound coverage for services Medicare does not cover.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Expand access to Medicaid Buy-In so people can work without losing essential care.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Require coverage of emergency backup caregiving and transition support.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Reduce repetitive paperwork and duplicative disability reviews where the condition is permanent.

heading: 05 / Healthcare and Care for Life
text: Protect continuity when an individual moves between communities or across state lines.

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: The CARE Act will create a national Community Living Capital Fund to help nonprofit organizations, local governments, housing providers, and families build or preserve accessible community housing. The program will coordinate HUD housing resources, federal tax incentives, local land, nonprofit investment, and Medicaid-funded services.

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Federal support should be flexible enough to help create different options because adults with disabilities do not all need or want the same living arrangement.

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Small homes shared by a limited number of residents

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Supported apartments with staff available on site

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Mixed-income and mixed-ability developments

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Independent apartments with visiting support

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: Residences designed for people with more significant medical or behavioral needs

heading: 06 / Building More Places Like Casa Familia
text: The standard must be dignity, safety, individual choice, and meaningful connection to the surrounding community. Community living cannot become institutional care with a nicer sign out front.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: One coordinated promise replaces a patchwork of disconnected programs. Here is the difference for families living it every day.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: One CARE Advocate coordinates the entire plan.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Community services can depend on a waiting list.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Necessary lifelong supports are guaranteed on a timely basis.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Succession and emergency planning begin during adolescence.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Housing, services, transportation, and community programming are coordinated.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Parents worry about what happens when they die.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: A successor-care plan, stable housing, and a support team are already in place.

heading: 07 / What This Means for Families
text: Success is measured by safety, health, independence, relationships, purpose, and belonging.

heading: 08 / How the Federal Government Will Work Together
text: The CARE Act does not pretend that one existing agency can do everything. It gives each agency a clear responsibility and creates one coordinated system around the individual.

heading: 09 / Protecting Choice and Preventing Abuse
text: A stronger care system must also protect the rights of the people it serves. The CARE Act will include independent oversight, transparent reporting, background and training standards, accessible complaint procedures, protection against abuse and financial exploitation, and regular review of restrictive guardianships.

heading: 09 / Protecting Choice and Preventing Abuse
text: No housing provider, caregiver, guardian, or government agency should control a person's life simply because that person needs support. The individual's voice, preferences, safety, and right to live in the community must remain at the center of every decision.

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: The federal government will be required to report whether participants are actually living better lives. Measures will include:

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Continuity of healthcare and support services

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Preventable hospitalizations and emergency placements

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Employment, education, volunteering, or meaningful daily activity

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Personal choice and supported decision-making

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Caregiver stability and workforce retention

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Avoidance of unnecessary institutionalization

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Perfect paperwork and an isolated life is not success.

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: A parent's death will always be a profound personal loss. It should not also become a housing crisis, a healthcare crisis, and a caregiving crisis.

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: The CARE Act will help adults build stable lives, homes, relationships, routines, and support networks while their parents are still alive. It will make sure the people who know and care for them are not replaced by a frantic search for services after a crisis.

heading: 10 / Measuring What Matters
text: Independence does not mean facing life alone. It means having the support to live the fullest life possible.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: No. A CARE Advocate coordinates programs and protects continuity. The advocate does not automatically control legal, medical, or financial decisions. Supported decision-making and the individual's own choices remain central.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: No. It would make those programs work together. Medicaid would generally fund long-term care and community supports. Social Security would provide income support. HUD would support housing, and Medicare would continue covering eligible medical care.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: No. The plan expands choices. Some people may prefer an independent apartment, a mixed community, a small shared home, a residence near family, or a community designed around specialized support. The individual's needs and preferences should guide the decision.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: Planning and transition begin early. The adult develops relationships with caregivers, the CARE Advocate, community programs, and future supporters before a crisis occurs. Parents remain partners, but they are no longer the entire system.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: The CARE Act coordinates existing federal programs and adds targeted investments in community care, housing, the caregiving workforce, technology, and family support. Preventing avoidable hospitalizations, homelessness, emergency placements, and unnecessary institutional care can also reduce costly crises.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: The legislation will establish functional and clinical eligibility for individuals with significant lifelong intellectual, developmental, and other disabilities who require ongoing support. Eligibility must be clear, fair, and portable across states.

heading: 11 / Frequently Asked Questions
text: Families should not have to spend a lifetime worrying about what happens next. The CARE Act creates a clear promise of lifelong care, housing, healthcare, dignity, and belonging.

heading: College ready. Trade ready. Life ready.
text: Every student deserves a pathway to purpose. The BUILD Act prepares students for the economy of tomorrow by connecting education to real careers, expanding apprenticeships, supporting teachers, rewarding innovation, and building the workforce America needs to compete.

heading: 01 / Why It Matters
text: America cannot compete in tomorrow's economy with yesterday's education system. The BUILD Act recognizes that human capacity is infrastructure.

heading: Stronger Economy
text: Investing in people strengthens our economy, grows small businesses, and improves national competitiveness.

heading: Higher Wages
text: Skills and credentials create higher-paying career paths and increase lifetime earning potential.

heading: More Opportunity
text: Expanding access to education and training opens doors for every student and every community.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Nine ways the BUILD Act builds America's workforce. Tap any item to expand.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Federal incentive grants reward school districts that develop career pathways in AI, cybersecurity, healthcare, advanced manufacturing, logistics, infrastructure, entrepreneurship, aerospace, and the skilled trades.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Every student graduates college ready, trade ready, entrepreneurially ready, or workforce ready through certifications, dual enrollment, apprenticeships, and career pathways.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Educational assistance for trade school, college, graduate school, and professional school in exchange for service in designated national priority industries.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Expand and modernize loan forgiveness for teachers, nurses, first responders, military personnel, public defenders, and other public service professionals.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Competitive federal grants reward districts that embrace innovation, workforce readiness, measurable outcomes, and industry partnerships.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Enhanced grants for districts investing in teacher compensation, teacher retention, mentoring, and professional development. Teachers are America's first responders for the future.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Accomplished professionals including engineers, physicians, scientists, entrepreneurs, artists, musicians, architects, attorneys, journalists, software developers, skilled trades professionals, veterans, and researchers may co-teach advanced courses for one semester. Certified teachers remain the teacher of record while BUILD Fellows contribute real-world expertise.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: National recognition and additional grant eligibility for school districts demonstrating exceptional workforce preparation and student success.

heading: 02 / The BUILD Act Solution
text: Increase funding for Historically Black Colleges and Universities and other colleges that provide education to underserved communities.

heading: 03 / Why BUILD Works
text: Higher wages create higher tax revenues.

heading: 03 / Why BUILD Works
text: More apprenticeships reduce workforce shortages.

heading: 03 / Why BUILD Works
text: Public-private partnerships maximize taxpayer investment.

heading: 03 / Why BUILD Works
text: Reward results instead of imposing mandates.

heading: Teachers are America's first responders for the future.
text: Police officers respond when communities are in crisis. Firefighters respond when buildings are burning. Emergency medical personnel respond when lives are in immediate danger. Teachers respond before those crises ever occur by preparing the next generation with the knowledge, discipline, critical thinking, and character that strengthen our communities and our economy.

heading: Teachers are America's first responders for the future.
text: Every student deserves a pathway to purpose.

heading: On the Issues
text: Gas is $5 a gallon, rent is half your paycheck, and every trip to the grocery store gets more expensive. For far too many neighbors, this has been the reality for far too long.

heading: On the Issues
text: Oliver Gilbert lived these challenges growing up in Miami Gardens, working his way through college and law school, and leading our city as Mayor and County Commissioner.

heading: On the Issues
text: What do President Trump and Washington Republicans do to help during these tough times? They spend your money on a war you didn’t ask for, didn’t vote for, and don’t need. They build a billion dollar ballroom for the Mar-a-Lago crowd. And they even use your own money to lie right to your face, spending millions on TV ads to deny the truth and divide our communities.

heading: On the Issues
text: South Florida families have had enough. It’s time to Put People First.

heading: Healthcare For All
text: We’re the richest country on earth, but we send billions of dollars to other countries so they can afford universal healthcare. How does that make sense? In Congress, Oliver will fight for a pathway to ensure that healthcare is a right for every American.

heading: Eliminate Income Taxes for Working Families
text: Families who are working hard to make ends meet shouldn’t have to carry the same tax burden as billionaires. The IRS should be spending more time auditing the ultra-wealthy than scrutinizing an Uber driver’s gas deduction. Oliver supports common sense tax policies indexed to what families in our communities actually earn, so that relief reaches the people who need it most and keeps money in working people’s hands.

heading: Stop ICE Raids Now
text: Our government has shamefully spent billions ripping families apart. They said ICE would only target criminals, but every day more and more hardworking people are being arrested and deported, often leaving young children behind to fend for themselves or leaving the only country they’ve ever known. It’s time to end funding for these shameful deportation policies and redirect that investment where it belongs: into our communities.

heading: Universal Childcare & Pre-K
text: Countries around the world have made universal childcare a reality. As a father, Oliver knows the challenges families are facing every day. In Washington, he will redirect spending toward our children and families, so that the resources no longer being wasted on mass deportations start building something that actually lasts.

heading: Expand Rapid Transit
text: In Congress, Oliver will fight to secure the federal funding needed to ensure the job gets done, and that our residents get the transit solutions they’ve been promised for decades.

heading: Investing in Jobs & Job Training
text: Oliver will fight in Washington to reinvest in job training, especially in high-paying technical fields that can’t easily be taken away by AI, and to strengthen support for entrepreneurs and small business owners.

heading: From Miami Gardens
text: I grew up here. I went to school here. I served here. And every step of that journey is the reason I’m running.

heading: From Miami Gardens
text: I was raised in Miami Gardens by two people who didn’t always see the world the same way. My mom was a Seventh-day Adventist teacher. My dad was a Baptist preacher. And in our house, I learned something early: people don’t have to agree on everything to love each other, to build a life together, to raise a family together.

heading: From Miami Gardens
text: They respected each other. They built something. That stayed with me.

heading: Every Step in This Community
text: Parkview Elementary. Parkway Middle. Miami Norland Senior High School. Every year of K through 12 happened right here. The teachers who taught me, the neighbors who watched me grow up, the friends who became family — they’re the reason I’m running, and they’re who I’m running for.

heading: Tallahassee
text: Florida A&M was my first real test. There were nights I lived out of my car. The work ethic and faith I brought from home are the only reasons I made it through. I learned that hardship isn’t something to perform — it’s something you live through, and what you do after defines you.

heading: What Did You Learn Today?
text: Law school meant a commute. I’d ride the 27 bus all the way down 27th Avenue to the Martin Luther King Metrorail station, then take the train to Coral Gables for class at the University of Miami School of Law. Some nights I’d get back late. And my dad would meet me at the MLK station. Every time. And he’d ask me one question.

heading: “What did you learn today?”
text: He wasn’t asking for himself. He wanted the knowledge to come back home. That question shaped everything I’ve done since.

heading: Mayor of Miami Gardens
text: I had the honor of serving as Mayor of my hometown for eight years. We worked on what mattered: safer neighborhoods, more parks, real economic growth, the kind of community policing that builds trust instead of breaking it. In 2020, Miami Gardens was named an All-America City — the first time in our history. I’m proud of that. But I’m more proud of what made it possible: a community that decided to invest in itself.

heading: County Commission Chair
text: On the County Commission, I’ve focused on a new goal: Make Miami-Dade County a truly world-class community. To get there, we have to overhaul our transportation system, which is why I’ve led bold initiatives to build up density along our transit corridors, creating partnerships that will fund rapid transit expansion and lead to more affordable housing in the neighborhoods that need it the most.

heading: Why I’m Running for Congress
text: What I’ve seen serving this community is simple. People want the same things. Good schools. Healthcare they can actually access. A commute that doesn’t take their life from them. A small business that can compete. A future their kids can build on.

heading: Why I’m Running for Congress
text: That’s what this campaign is about. Not running against anyone. Running toward something. Building a future that works for everyone, across South Florida.
